clue.text: Metal on the roof intermittently reflecting sunlight?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sheet metal sealing joints on a roof
second meaning: glinting on and off

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves read as one picture of a shiny roof, but each is a separate meaning of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders call the weatherproof strips around chimneys this, and anything glinting on and off is also doing it.

clue.text: Praise for two flips

indicators.note: a thing that flips turns over, so the word is read back to front

parts.note: dual means for two, as in dual controls

explanation.surface: Someone is applauded for two acrobatic flips.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is a formal verb meaning to praise highly.

clue.text: Gale ordered sweet and sour

indicators.note: a dish that is ordered is called for, and here the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Gale orders sweet and sour from a Chinese takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Gale looks like a diner's name; it is the definition, a strong wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou'wester is a south-westerly wind, which in Britain is often a stormy blow.

clue.text: Offspring lives with us, rising expenses primarily

parts.note: he lives here = he is here

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: primarily points to what comes first, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter of expenses

explanation.surface: A grown child moves back in with the parents, and the household costs go up.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal, legal word for a person's children or descendants.

clue.text: Miracle shot, dead on small target

parts.note: have a shot = have a go
D is the abbreviation for dead
S is the abbreviation for small
an end is an aim or target

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter lands a miracle shot dead on a tiny target.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected stroke of luck, as if sent from heaven, much like a miracle.

clue.text: A newspaper includes odd pieces in French to impress

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times

indicators.note: odd pieces means the first, third and fifth letters and so on are kept

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of French

explanation.surface: A newspaper slips some French phrases into its copy to look sophisticated.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the pink British business paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect someone is to make an impression on them, to move or influence them.

clue.text: Some people uncoupling at home

indicators.note: uncoupling separates a pair, so this short word is split apart for other letters to sit between

parts.note: taken as written
part = some of a whole
men = people

explanation.surface: Some couples are separating while still living at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncoupling seems to describe the people, but it tells you to prise the two letters of 'at' apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a self-contained dwelling, so it is a home.

clue.text: Take lift up, saving time with children

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is written from the bottom upwards
saving here means except, so that letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
CH is the abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: Instructions to take the lift up, saving time when you have children with you.
explanation.walkthrough: Lift is also a slang word for steal, which makes it tempting as the definition; Take is.
explanation.definitionFit: To filch is to pilfer or steal something small, so it means to take.

clue.text: Top doctor confining new sovereign to bed

indicators.note: confining something means shutting it inside, so these letters go within the outer word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
N is the abbreviation for new
a sultan is a Muslim sovereign

explanation.surface: A senior doctor orders a newly crowned monarch to stay in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a consultant is the most senior grade of specialist doctor.

clue.text: Nameless Cambridge college keeps university groups waiting

indicators.note: a thing that keeps something holds it inside
without a name means the abbreviation for name is removed

parts.note: Queens' is a Cambridge college
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: An anonymous Cambridge college holds on to university groups that are kept waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: N for name is dropped from the college before the U goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Queues are lines of people standing in turn, so they are groups waiting.

clue.text: Last date's reason for not phoning?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the final time by which something must be done
second meaning, read cryptically: a telephone line that is dead

explanation.walkthrough: Last date suggests a final romantic outing, and the question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is a time limit, and a dead line is a phone connection with no signal.

clue.text: The Spanish still travel abroad, bagging hotels at the last minute

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
even = still, as in even better

indicators.note: bagging something puts it inside a bag, so letters are held within

parts.note: to tour is to travel round a country
H is the abbreviation for hotel, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Spaniards still go on foreign trips, booking hotels at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Hs go inside TOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh hour is an idiom for the latest possible moment before a deadline.

clue.text: Words very old police force eschews on street

indicators.note: to eschew is to avoid or do without, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old
a constabulary is a police force
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Words to the effect that a very old-fashioned police force no longer patrols the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: ON and ST are both taken out of the police force word.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocabulary is the stock of words a person or language uses.

clue.text: Note doctor performs operation in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
acts = performs
OP is short for operation

explanation.surface: A memo reports a surgeon doing an operation backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcard is a short card for sending a brief message, a kind of note.

clue.text: Sailor on land entertained by ship paintings

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so letters sit inside another piece

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a ship
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: A sailor ashore is welcomed aboard a vessel to view its art.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstracts are non-representational paintings, works of abstract art.

clue.text: Bother, wrong name on back of certificate

indicators.note: the back of a word is its tail end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of certificate
a cross marks a wrong answer
to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: Annoyance at a misspelt name on a certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: Bother looks like an exclamation of annoyance but is a verb here; on means the X and CITE come after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite can mean to agitate or stir up, close to bother in the sense of disturb.

clue.text: Baby-sitting circle had parties

indicators.note: people who party go wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A babysitting group of parents threw some parties.
explanation.walkthrough: A babysitting circle is a group of parents who mind each other's children.
explanation.definitionFit: Childcare is looking after children, which is what babysitting is.

clue.text: Corpulent swimmer taking short walk at reduced speed

indicators.note: something short is cut off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reduced means made smaller, so the last letter is trimmed

parts.note: rush = speed

explanation.surface: A fat swimmer takes a slow, brief stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: The walrus is a huge, blubbery marine mammal, so a fat creature that swims.

clue.text: Feeding ten, I turn to mince

indicators.note: mincing chops things into small bits, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook catering for ten decides to mince some meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a nourishing substance, so it is feeding in the noun sense of food.

clue.text: 'Please leave' picked up very loudly from football supporter?

indicators.note: in a down entry picked up means lifted, so the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud
of = from, as in a man of Kent
a fan is a supporter

explanation.surface: A football supporter's shout to the referee to go away, heard loud and clear.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff off is a mild British euphemism for a ruder dismissal; 'Please' is sarcastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff off is a British slang command telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Shiver cycling racers in Yorkshire town

indicators.note: cycling suggests going round, so the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: shudder = shiver
the field is all the competitors in a race

explanation.surface: Cyclists shiver as they race through a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling looks like part of the race scene; it moves the S to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Huddersfield is a large town in West Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Deal with a druggie

parts.note: to do a task is to deal with it
per = a, as in twice a day

explanation.surface: An instruction to handle a drug addict.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal looks like drug dealing; with is the link and the second word of the phrase deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: A doper is a slang term for someone who takes drugs.

clue.text: Log you could make treen from

indicators.note: making something new out of material means the letters are reworked into another word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woodworker notes that a log could be turned into treen.
explanation.walkthrough: Treen is small wooden household ware; Log is a verb meaning record.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data is to record it, which is what logging means.

clue.text: I'm doubtful magistrate has secured vault

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside

parts.note: JP, Justice of the Peace, is a magistrate
um is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that a magistrate has locked a strongroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Vault looks like a strongroom in the surface, but it is the verb, to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To vault over something is to leap over it, so it means jump.

clue.text: Half staring chap cooked duck soup

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed up
only half of the word is kept, so the rest is dropped

parts.note: gazing = staring
taken as written
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A goggle-eyed fellow makes duck soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck looks like an ingredient; it is the cricket zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazpacho is a cold Spanish soup made from raw tomatoes and vegetables.

clue.text: China reported Asian hardwood now more expensive

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we use the sound

parts.note: teak is a hardwood from south-east Asia
prices are up

explanation.surface: A report that China's tropical timber has risen in price.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the country; it is crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacup is a piece of china, porcelain tableware for drinking from.

clue.text: Out of intransigency Prussia split part of Europe

indicators.note: out of means the letters are drawn from within the following words

parts.note: the end of intransigency and the start of Prussia

explanation.surface: Stubbornness causes Prussia to break away from the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is an island member state of the European Union, so counts as part of Europe.

clue.text: Wasting billions, perhaps Trident alarm sounds permanently

indicators.note: wasting means losing or throwing away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a trident is a three-pronged fork, one example
B is the abbreviation for billions
an alarm beeps

explanation.surface: Billions spent on Trident nuclear missiles set alarm bells ringing for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is Britain's nuclear missile system, so the surface is about defence spending; here it is just a pronged fork.
explanation.definitionFit: For keeps is an idiom meaning forever, to keep permanently.
